subject: general
question: Sodium or potassium salt of long chain carboxylic acid is known as which of the following?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Soap**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Sodium or potassium salts of long chain carboxylic acids are commonly referred to as **soaps**.
 
• Soaps are produced through a chemical process called **saponification**, where fats and oils react with a base.
 
• In the saponification process, triglycerides (fats/oils) are hydrolyzed to produce glycerol and soap.
 
• Soaps are effective in cleaning because they are surfactants, which means they lower the surface tension of water, allowing it to mix with oils and dirt.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Micelle**:

 
 
• A micelle is an aggregate of surfactant molecules dispersed in a liquid colloid forming a molecular assembly.
 
• Micelles are formed when the concentration of surfactant molecules exceeds the critical micelle concentration (CMC).
 
• They play a key role in the cleansing action of soaps and detergents by trapping grease and dirt.
 
 
 
• **Detergents**:
 
 
• Detergents are synthetic cleaning agents, typically made from petrochemicals.
 
• Unlike soaps, detergents can perform well in hard water as they do not form scum.
 
• Detergents are also surfactants and work by emulsifying oils and dirt.
 
 
 
• **Saponification**:
 
 
• Saponification is a chemical reaction that produces soap from fats/oils and an alkali.
 
• The reaction results in the formation of glycerol and soap.
 
• This process is crucial in traditional soap making and industrial soap production.
 
 
 
• **Surfactants**:
 
 
• Surfactants are compounds that lower the surface tension between two liquids or a liquid and a solid.
 
• They are the active agents in soaps and detergents that enable them to clean effectively.
 
• Surfactants can be classified as anionic, cationic, nonionic, or amphoteric based on their charge.
